Andermatt Swiss Alps launches alpine riverside plots for international buyers, priced from CHF15 mil
article:
Andermatt Swiss Alps (ASA) has launched The Villas, a collection of four riverside land plots in Andermatt, Switzerland, with prices starting from CHF15 million ($23.2 million) per plot.

Backed by Orascom Development, The Villas offers one of the few legally secure opportunities for non-resident nationals to own real estate in Switzerland, according to a press release by Andermatt Swiss Alps.

Starting from 1,800 sq m (19,375 sq ft), the plots are first sold as land only, before buyers will spend another CHF15 million to CHF20 million to build a premium villa on each plot, according to the developer.

Looking to invest in overseas properties ? Explore projects available for sale around the world

The homes can exceed 1,000 sq m (10,764 sq ft), as Andermatt is exempt from two Swiss property restrictions, said Andermatt Swiss Alps. The Lex Koller exemption allows international buyers the same ownership rights as Swiss nationals until 2040, while the Lex Weber exemption allows new second homes to be developed.

Buyers can commission their own homes

Each buyer can determine the floor plan and interiors of the residence within Andermatt's design parameters.

They may appoint their own architects and designers or work with design firms and designers including Snøhetta, Pierre Yovanovitch and Patricia Urquiola.  Andermatt Swiss Alps will manage the construction and delivery of the property with the owner's chosen team.

“The Villas will be a truly unique residential offering we have brought to Asia,” says Maureen Yeo, regional director for Asia at Andermatt Swiss Alps. “Each residence is individually commissioned and delivered by ASA to the owner’s vision, making every home truly one of a kind.”

Owners will also have access to services including housekeeping, property management, butler service, in-villa dining, a house car and chauffeur. The residential services programme includes access to luxury alpine resort The Chedi Andermatt and the upcoming The Alpinist hotel and residences.

Part of the Andermatt Reuss development

The four plots are located along the Reuss River at an elevation of 1,444m, and located about 90 minutes from Zürich and 2.5 hours from Milan.

The Villas forms part of the CHF2 billion Andermatt Reuss masterplan, which comprises 42 apartment buildings and six hotels. Other amenities include an 18-hole golf course and the 650-seat Andermatt Concert Hall.

The wider Andermatt-Sedrun-Disentis ski area has more than 180km of connected terrain, reaching elevations of up to 3,000m.

Residential buildings within The Villas will be built to the Minergie standard, Switzerland's sustainable construction standard, with electricity and heat supplied entirely from renewable sources.

title: Hong Kong converts hotels into student dorms
article:
Late last month, an open tender for Hotel Cozi Harbour View in Kwun Tong was announced, with interested parties given until Oct 15 to submit bids.

The 598-room hotel, located in Hong Kong’s eastern Kowloon Peninsula, a former industrial area, was taken over by Nanyang Commercial Bank for HK$1.87 billion (US$238.4 million) in 2025, with the bank now looking to dispose of the asset to the highest bidder.

Just a week after the announcement of the tender, Nina Hospitality, one of the largest hotel operators in Hong Kong, unveiled the completion of the HK$120 million renovation at Nina Hotel Island South.

The refurbishment transformed the hotel’s lobby and guestrooms and launched both balcony suites and family rooms.

It is the second major refurbishment project of the hospitality arm of private developer Chinachem Group, following the renovation of guest rooms at its flagship Nina Hotel Tsuen Wan West, completed in 2024.

The renovation of Tsuen Wan’s lobbies is still under way, with the group earmarking HK$225 million for the project, part of Nina Hospitality’s rebranding announced in 2021.

The two investment strategies illustrate contrasting outlooks for Hong Kong’s hotel industry.

The city consistently held the crown as the world’s most-visited city before 2019, according to consultancy Euromonitor International.

With 29.26 million overnight visitor arrivals in 2018, Hong Kong’s hotels saw their average occupancy rate increase by 2 percentage points to 91% that year, according to the Tourism Commission.

In 2025, Hong Kong saw 23.19 million overnight visitor arrivals, according to official data, still 20% below their 2018 peak. The average hotel room occupancy rate, meanwhile, was at 87%.

It is no surprise that with higher financing costs, brought about by an increase in interest rates, many asset owners found the hotel business challenging. Those who were unable to service debts had to dispose of their assets, either by selling them at huge discounts or facing asset liquidation by their creditors, recent cases have shown.

Many of these hotels sold were acquired by new owners for conversion into student accommodation.

So far this year, Hong Kong has recorded HK$8.2 billion worth of hotel property deals involving about 2,550 rooms, according to Colliers. Most of these transactions were for student accommodation conversions, and some were a hybrid of co-living – targeted towards students or young professionals – and hotel offerings, the property consultancy added.

With the government’s bid to turn Hong Kong into a global education hub, JLL estimated that the city faced a shortfall of more than 140,000 student beds by the 2029-2030 school year.

“For investors, the sector presents a compelling opportunity underpinned by resilient demand and income visibility that is largely insulated from broader real estate market cycles,” said Cathie Chung, senior director of research at JLL Hong Kong.

For Nina Hospitality, refurbishing its hotels was a way to prepare for higher accommodation demand from tourists, managing director Simon Manning said.

“While recovery is slower than pre-pandemic levels, we are encouraged by the government’s initiatives such as mega-events, sports-related programmes and efforts to attract new markets, which are driving positive momentum,” Manning said.

“By upgrading our hotels and services, we ensure Nina Hospitality is optimally positioned to capture demand and exceed guest expectations as tourism continues to strengthen.”

Since the 50,000-seat Kai Tak Stadium in Kowloon opened in March last year, the mammoth venue had “quickly emerged as one of Asia’s leading event venues and top three internationally in terms of ticket sales in its first year”, according to Colliers.

In the first half of the year, about 1.75 million visitors were drawn to more than 130 events in Hong Kong, generating around HK$5.8 billion in spending and contributing HK$3.3 billion to the economy, according to Financial Secretary Paul Chan Mo-po.

As the city also books global performers amid a growing demand for student accommodation, the hotel property industry was likely to see more hotel conversions and also investment in existing and new hotels, analysts said.

In particular, hotels in the higher market segment could see more capital deployment to refresh and improve their amenities, while well-priced midscale assets could be primed for student accommodation conversions, said Shaman Chellaram, senior director for hotel advisory and valuation and advisory services at Colliers.

“Each segment caters to different demand drivers and end-users with very distinct operating and business models,” Chellaram said.

Location might determine whether a hotel was suitable for a student dormitory asset or a tourist accommodation, said Cleavon Tan, senior vice-president of hotels and hospitality group at JLL Hong Kong.

“Hotels in established tourism and business districts, with strong demand drivers, can offer a compelling case for continued hotel use and further investment,” Tan said.

“For properties outside these core locations, particularly where hotel performance is weaker but access to universities and public transport is good, student accommodation may offer a more attractive use. A location that is less competitive for tourists can still work well for students.”

title: Seven industrial units in Tagore and one Kovan HDB shop on the market for $21 mil
article:
Seven freehold strata Business 1 (B1) light industrial units at Tag A in the Tagore Industrial Estate as well as a ground-floor HDB shop on Hougang Street 21 in Kovan have been offered for sale with a total guide price of $21 million.

At Tag A, the seven industrial units span about 22,238 sq ft of combined strata area across levels one, two and four.

They are fully leased to a diversified tenant mix, which can provide investors with immediate rental income while preserving the flexibility for future owner-occupation, said marketing agent Knight Frank Singapore.

Their combined guide price is $17.8 million, which is about $800 psf on strata area.

The seven strata units can be acquired individually or as a portfolio, and will be sold subject to their respective existing tenancies.

Developed by Master Contract Services, Tag A has a 5.95m floor-to-floor height and floor loading of 10 kilonewton per sq m, which can support a range of light industrial and business activities. Occupiers can also access lifestyle amenities including a 50m infinity pool, indoor gym and BBQ pavilions.

Tania Ong, senior manager at Knight Frank Singapore, said freehold B1 strata industrial units are “rarely available for sale”, with newer industrial developments typically offered on shorter leasehold tenures such as 30 years.

As for the Kovan HDB shop, the property carries a guide price of $3.2 million, which works out to around $3,764 psf on its strata area of 850 sq ft.

Located at Block 210 Hougang Street 21 , the unit is currently owner-occupied and may be sold with a leaseback arrangement.

It has a wide frontage and a regular, column-free layout. Subject to the relevant approvals, Knight Frank said there may be potential to subdivide the premises into two units or explore alternative uses.

With no living quarters attached, the property does not attract additional buyer’s stamp duty (ABSD).

The shop has sheltered access to Kovan MRT Station, Kovan Express Bus Terminal , and the nearby market and food centre.

“Ground-floor HDB shops priced below $5 million offer investors an accessible entry quantum into the commercial property market,” said Ong.

Both the Tag A industrial portfolio and the Kovan shop can be acquired by local and foreign investors, corporates and owner-occupiers.

The expression of interest exercise closes at 3pm on Oct 29 for the Tag A portfolio, and at 3pm on Nov 19 for the Kovan HDB shop.

title: Keppel Reit to sell Seoul CBD office building at KRW348.8 bil property value, 37.2% above purchase price
article:
Keppel Reit and Keppel Capital Investment Holdings will divest their respective stakes of 99.38% and 0.62% in T Tower, a freehold Grade A office building in Seoul’s CBD, to a real estate fund based in South Korea.

The agreed property value for 100% of the property is KRW348.8 billion (about $325.9 million).

That is at a 37.2% premium to the purchase price when T Tower was acquired in May 2019, and is also 7.4% above its valuation as at Aug 31 this year, in local currency terms.

This demonstrates Keppel Reit’s ability to "crystallise value", said Chua Hsien Yang, CEO of the Reit manager, in a Sept 23 exchange filing.

T Tower is a 28-storey building with a gross floor area of 41,598 sq m (about 447,757 sq ft). It was 92.1% occupied as at June 30. The building is near key retail districts such as Myeong-dong and Namdaemun, and is a five-minute walk from Seoul Station, the city's major railway station.

"Together with the recent divestment of KR Ginza II in Tokyo, the transaction underscores our strategic capital recycling capability, strengthens Keppel Reit’s balance sheet, and enhances the Reit’s financial flexibility," Chua noted.

The sale of T Tower is expected to be completed in 4Q2026.

Following these divestments, Singapore will make up 81.1% of Keppel Reit's portfolio value. This will continue to position the Reit to benefit from favourable office market fundamentals, including resilient occupier demand, limited upcoming CBD supply and the absence of significant new completions, according to Chua.

title: iX BIOPHARMA: Why Investors Are Paying S$600M for Future Value
article:
iX Biopharma's latest corporate presentation, prepared for the
23 Sept CITIC Securities International Investor Forum
, contains

several revealing details — especially when viewed against the extraordinary rise in iX's share price over the past year.

The
event
in Hong Kong was expected to attract more than 2,000 investors, policymakers, academics and business leaders across hundreds of one-on-one and group meetings.

The iX team comprised Chairman & CEO Eddy Lee, Chief Commercial Officer Eva Tan and Business Development Manager Daniel Chow.
In its presentation deck, iX itself highlights its stock's extraordinary rerating.

Available on the SGX website, the
deck
shows the shares rising from roughly
2 cents
in Sept 2025 to
above 60 cents
in Sept 2026 — around a 30-fold increase. Market capitalisation had reached about
S$629 million
as at 17 Sept.
Source: iX Biopharma

Paying S$600M for future value

Paying S$600M for future value

Paying S$600M for future value

A year ago, iX was valued like a distressed small biotech, with an interesting technology to deliver drugs through wafers placed under the tongue.
Today, investors are paying more than S$600 million for future success — principally Wafermine and, to a lesser extent, the wider WaferiX platform and US compounding opportunity.

So judging iX simply by its current revenue or near-term PE ratio misses the point.

The stock is increasingly being valued on the probability that Wafermine becomes a valuable late-stage pharmaceutical asset — plus some value for the US compounding opportunity.

Eddy Lee, Founder, Chairman & CEO of IX Biopharma

Why the huge value potential

Why the huge value potential

iX points investors towards actual transactions occurring in non-opioid pain.

The presentation highlights Eli Lilly's
acquisition
of SiteOne Therapeutics for
up to US$1 billion
, despite its lead non-opioid pain drug being only Phase 2-ready.
Importantly, the US$1 billion is not all upfront cash: it includes an undisclosed initial payment plus future regulatory and commercial milestone payments.
iX also cites
AbbVie's deal
worth up to
US$745 million
for two early-stage pain assets. US$30 million was paid upfront, with most of the potential value dependent on the drugs successfully reaching future milestones.
And iX notes analyst estimates of
US$2–4 billion peak sales
for Vertex's newly approved non-opioid pain drug
Journavx
.

Journavx
(suzetrigine) is a much more relevant comparison because it treats the same broad indication as iX's Wafermine: moderate-to-severe acute pain.

FDA
approved
Journavx
in January 2025, making it the first approved drug in a new class of non-opioid pain medicine.

Wafermine offers a different product profile.

Journavx is an oral tablet. Wafermine is a
sublingual ketamine wafer
designed to enter the bloodstream rapidly.

iX cites

Wafermine onset of 10–20 minutes

versus

Journavx's 1–2 hours.

If its Phase 3 is successful, Wafermine could be particularly valuable in:

emergency medicine;

postoperative acute pain;

battlefield medicine;

situations where rapid relief is important but injection is undesirable.

iX is showing that Big Pharma really is paying substantial sums for promising non-opioid pain assets.

This implies that a successful Phase 3 Wafermine could potentially attract a large pharmaceutical partner or buyer.

Core Wafermine story remains intact

iX says the US government will provide about
US$41 million
for the Phase 3 and Emergency Use Authorization (EUA) programme.
Importantly, this funding reduces the need for shareholder dilution, while iX retains the rights and product sponsorship.

The regulatory sequence also remains unchanged.

The military emergency pathway has been opened, but Wafermine's EUA submission itself is still pending.
After submission come FDA EUA approval and, if granted, the commencement of military supply.

Meanwhile, on the conventional commercial pathway, the next milestones remain
-- FDA Type C meeting (to clarify the trial parameters),
-- Phase 3 commencement,
-- Phase 3 topline results,
-- NDA (new drug application) filing for commercial sale and, ultimately,
-- potential out-licensing (big pharma commercialises it while paying agreed sums to iX).

title: Bond sell-off deepens as Fed rate-hike bets build
article:
(Sept 24): A global sell-off in bonds intensified, jolting investors as robust US economic data and weak demand at a debt auction drove Treasury yields across much of the curve to their highest levels in almost two decades.

The bruising losses on Wall Street swept into Asia Pacific with bonds sliding in Japan, Australia and New Zealand. The US 10-year yield surged 15 basis points to 5.11% Wednesday, its biggest increase since the turmoil triggered by US President Donald Trump’s April 2025 tariff announcement. Weak demand at a sale of US five-year notes pushed the yield above 5% for the first time since 2007.

There was little respite for bond traders in Asia as Japan’s 10-year borrowing cost climbed to the highest since 1996. Its Australian counterpart posted the steepest increase in almost two weeks, while New Zealand’s equivalent recorded its biggest jump since early March.

Some relief came from oil, with Brent paring Wednesday’s rally to trade 0.6% lower at around US$102.50 a barrel.

Elsewhere, MSCI’s gauge of Asian stocks fell 0.4%, though Japanese shares rallied 1.4% as traders returned from a three-day holiday. Chinese equities edged lower at the open as President Xi Jinping arrived in America for his first state visit in 11 years. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent announced earlier that the US and China sealed a two-month extension to their trade truce.

The prospect of higher energy costs colliding with a still-strong US economy is adding pressure to a bond market already rattled by weak auction demand and concerns that interest rates will stay elevated. As Treasury yields surged, traders ramped up bets on further Federal Reserve (Fed) tightening following last week’s first rate increase since 2023.

See also: Asian stocks rise after US tech rally, oil drops

“This is the market telling us we’ve entered a genuine re-tightening cycle,” said Tony Miano at Wells Fargo Investment Institute. “The entire curve is repricing at once, which means higher discount rates for equities, higher mortgage and corporate borrowing costs, and a higher bar for risk assets.”

Officials raised borrowing costs last week to a range of 3.75% to 4%, a move Fed chair Kevin Warsh said removed a “dose of accommodation”. Fed governor Michael Barr said further rate hikes are likely needed to return inflation to the central bank’s 2% target.

Swaps now fully reflect three quarter-point hikes over the next year, with significant hedging for a fourth. If realised, that would take the central bank’s target rate into a range of 4.75% to 5%.

See also: Asian stocks climb after tech powers Wall Street

In other corners of the market, gold held its losses from the previous session, when bullion fell 1.7% to about US$4,290 an ounce. The non-yielding commodity’s appeal lessens as interest rates rise.

US diesel futures jumped as the Trump administration worked with refiners to voluntarily curb exports of the product as an alternative to an outright ban on overseas shipments.

Meanwhile, data showed US mortgage rates climbed to a more than two-year high, while the S&P Global flash US composite purchasing managers index rose in September to its highest since July 2021, signalling faster growth in business activity.

In a new set of rate projections released after last week’s decision, Fed officials pencilled in another increase before the end of the year, according to the median forecast. The median projection for 2027 pointed to no additional rate hikes next year, though eight officials saw their benchmark rate ending next year half a point higher than current levels.

“After the monetary policy meetings, there was a sense that bond yields might settle down, so the speed of the latest rise feels quite rapid,” said Ikuo Mitsui, a fund manager at Aizawa Securities Co. “That said, yields are reaching fairly attractive levels, and bond investors may now start looking for opportunities to put money to work.”
• Meta Platforms Inc unveiled a palm-sized, dedicated gadget for using Muse, the company’s popular new artificial intelligence assistant, pushing deeper into the AI devices market with a surprise announcement.
• Walt Disney Co is raising prices on several of its streaming subscriptions in the US for the sixth time in as many years.
• McDonald’s Corp is earmarking roughly US$8.5 billion to help franchisees implement a multiyear plan to serve better food, improve service and make restaurants easier to run.
